CARRIED FORWARD FROM nyc.v2.8. Demo-scoped corrected subset. Structure follows the nyc.v2 draft (rules/proposals/); every fact carries a verification status and an evidence reference into docs/VERIFICATION-SOURCES.md. CHANGE FROM nyc.v2.7. THIS BUMP CARRIES A REGULATORY CORRECTION AND MOVES EVALUATED OUTPUT. It changes exactly one rule, DOB-ASSEMBLY-001, and its deadline only. UNIT. The TPA filing lead moves from published_minimum / calendar_days 10 to business_days_minimum / business_days 10. The unit is BUSINESS days on two independent primary sources: TPPN #07/96, 'at least ten (10) business days in advance of the planned event', and NYC Admin Code Table 28-112.8, 'at least ten work days prior to the event'. The calendar reading it replaces came from one weaker source, DOB Code Notes (12.2016): that document says '10 days' and never says 'calendar', disclaims itself as 'only a summary and overview ... not intended to substitute for the full text and meaning of any law, rule or regulation', names TPPN #07/96 as the governing notice, and describes the pre-DOB-NOW borough-office filing process. DOB's bulletin index annotates other 1996 notices RESCINDED or superseded; #07/96 carries no such annotation, so it was not treated as withdrawn. No new deadline type was invented: business_days_minimum already exists and DOB-TENT-001, SLA-ONEDAY-001 and SLA-CATERING-001 already use it. BOUNDARY. exclusive becomes inclusive. 'At least ten (10)' admits day ten, and DOB's current filing page adds that the filing date of the online request counts as one of the days. WHY THEY LAND TOGETHER, which is the load-bearing part of this bump. Measured on Scenario F (event 2026-08-11) against the fixture calendar: the value this file previously published dated the deadline 2026-07-31; the boundary correction ALONE would date it 2026-08-01; both corrections together date it 2026-07-28. Publishing the boundary by itself would therefore have moved the deadline one day LATER than a value already known to be wrong, in the direction that tells an organizer they have more time than they do, while the sources put it three days EARLIER. Splitting this into two bumps would have shipped a strictly worse artifact in between, and BASELINE.md's immutability rule means each would have been its own published version with its own row. So they are one publish. THE THREE-BUSINESS-DAY FLOOR IS PUBLISHED AS TEXT, NOT AS MATH. deadline.display now carries both constraints and distinguishes them: ten business days is the FEE trigger (filing inside it adds the per-day surcharge), while three business days or less before the EVENT is whether the filing is processed at all. The floor is anchored to the event and not to the ten-day deadline. It is prose in display, following PARKS-EVENT-001's single-string precedent, because no deadline type in popengine-rules/v2 expresses a business-day floor; adding a field or a type to express one is a schema change and needs its own approved spec, so this file states the fact rather than inventing a shape for it. NOTES. The old note described a branch on venue_has_assembly_approval that no trigger evaluates. It is replaced by the statute the coverage question actually rests on, AC 28-117.1.3 (Local Law 2/2013), quoted rather than paraphrased, together with an explicit statement that whether an existing place-of-assembly certificate removes the temporary filing is NOT PUBLISHED in either direction. The note asserts no exemption and no requirement-by-implication; the unknown-collapse claim the old note carried had no source and is removed rather than softened. The trigger still reads location_type and headcount only, so venue_has_assembly_approval remains collected and unread (issue #89, reopened). VERIFICATION. DOB-ASSEMBLY-001's verification.qualification no longer says 'lead wording variance', because the variance is resolved; it now states only what remains unestablished, which is narrower: whether a TPA is required at all at a venue that already holds a place-of-assembly certificate, and whether the 75-on-a-roof-terrace threshold reaches TEMPORARY filings specifically. Both are silence in the sources, not conflict between them. SLA-ONEDAY-001 AND SLA-CATERING-001: RECORDED, NOT CHANGED. Both carried an UNQUALIFIED SOURCE_CONFIRMED while three official sources disagree on the unit — sla.ny.gov's permit page says 15 BUSINESS days (docs/VERIFICATION-SOURCES.md line 61), businessexpress.ny.gov says 15 DAYS, and an SLA-hosted, still-linked legacy PDF says 15 DAYS; ABC Law §97 and §98 and the located parts of 9 NYCRR Part 29 are silent. Each verification block now records that conflict. No type, value or boundary moves on either rule: 15 business_days is kept because it comes from the agency's own current page for the current instrument, and because it is the longer and therefore safer window. WHAT THIS DEADLINE NOW RENDERS IN PRODUCTION. business_days_minimum needs the holiday list config.business_day_math pins, and that list is deliberately unpublished (SPEC-CONFLICT #130; the decision and its evidence are recorded in apps/api/src/calendar.ts), so DOB-ASSEMBLY-001 renders NOT_CALCULABLE with a null latest_apply_date and 'confirm with agency' wherever the api evaluates it. The fixture suite injects an empty holiday list and therefore computes 2026-07-28 for Scenario F. That divergence is by design and is stated here so nobody reads a green suite as evidence that this rule dates correctly in the running product. It errs toward under-claiming rather than over-claiming: NOT_CALCULABLE never counts toward FEASIBLE. THE FEE LINE STATED A VENUE'S ANNUAL PERMIT AS IF IT WERE AN EVENT COST. fee.display read 'TPA min $250; FDNY assembly permit from $415 (75-149 occupancy)'. The $415 is real and correctly cited — 2022 Fire Code Appendix A, FC A03.1(4), 'Occupancy 75 to 149 $415.00' — but FC 105.6 attaches it to the permit 'to establish and operate a place of assembly', term 'not to exceed 1 year'. That is the party operating the space, not the organizer booking it for one night, so publishing it beside the TPA presented a venue's recurring cost as part of this event's price. The Fire Code's temporary-event line is a different item, A03.1(68) 'Street fairs and other public gatherings or gathering places' at $210 per hour, and DOB's page links the terminology ('also referred to in the Fire Code as a public gathering'). WHICH LINE FDNY BILLS FOR A ONE-OFF TPA EVENT IS NOT PUBLISHED — not in Appendix A, not in Fire Code Chapter 1, and not on FDNY's Public Assembly Permit page, which says only 'Fee varies based on the number of occupants'. So the fee was NOT corrected by swapping one amount for another: it now publishes the DOB amounts, which are established, and states that FDNY's charge for a one-off event is not published as an amount. A NOTE ON THE PERIODICITY ARGUMENT, recorded because it is weaker than it first appears: A03.1's preamble says 'All such fees are per year, except when based on frequency of inspection or hourly rate, as indicated', and item (4)'s own sub-label is 'Fire safety inspection/permit (frequency of inspection as required by code or rule)' — which falls inside that exception. So the preamble does not establish that $415 is annual; FC 105.6's one-year permit term is what carries the point, and the note says so rather than asserting the stronger reading. Citations move to the 2022 Fire Code throughout: Local Law 47 of 2022 took effect 2022-04-15, FDNY states the 2014 edition is no longer in effect, and the 2014 appendix numbered these rows item (3). THE $250 IS DOB'S PUBLISHED FIGURE AND THE STATUTE LABELS IT DIFFERENTLY, which the file now records. In Table 28-112.8 the row literally named 'Temporary place of assembly certificate of operation' is $130, while the $250, the $100-per-day late fee AND the 'at least ten work days prior to the event' comment all sit together on the adjacent row named 'Temporary use letter for place of assembly'. Which row DOB NOW bills, or whether one filing draws both, is NOT ESTABLISHED; no 1 RCNY rule reconciling them was located, and AC 28-112.1 leaves room for one ('prescribed herein or in rules'). DOB's public TPA page publishes $250 as the fee an applicant pays and that is what this file displays. The same row-label caveat is now recorded against this rule's second source for the ten-day unit, because the 'ten work days' comment is on the 'Temporary use letter' row rather than the row bearing the TPA's own name — TPPN #07/96 is unaffected and remains an independent source for the unit. THE ROOF-TERRACE THRESHOLD CARRIED NO 20-FOOT QUALIFIER AND OVERCLAIMED. The note read 'Thresholds: 75+ indoors OR ON ROOF TERRACES; 200+ outdoors', which follows DOB's webpage bullet. The code does not: BC 303.7(1) sweeps in 'open spaces at 20 feet (6096 mm) or more above or below grade plane, such as roofs or roof terraces', so a roof under 20 feet above grade plane is not on the 75-person indoor side at all and BC 303.7(2)'s 200-person outdoor threshold governs it. The qualifier is now quoted in the note. THE REACH TO THE TEMPORARY INSTRUMENT IS ALSO NOW ESTABLISHED IN CODE TEXT rather than resting on a DOB webpage sentence, which is what this rule's verification block previously listed as unestablished: AC 28-111.6 states the TPA trigger as 'the temporary use of space as a place of assembly', the 2022 Building Code Chapter 2 definition of PLACE OF ASSEMBLY resolves that term 'when such use requires a place of assembly Certificate of Operation pursuant to Section 303.7', and 303.7 classifies the SPACE with no permanent/temporary distinction. The Fire Code adopts the same definition ('as regulated by the Building Code'). That qualification is therefore withdrawn as resolved rather than left standing. WHAT THE 20-FOOT QUALIFIER MEANS FOR THE TRIGGER, AND WHY THIS BUMP DOES NOT ACT ON IT. The qualifier makes the rooftop threshold conditional on height above grade plane, which this ruleset does not collect and no trigger reads: the trigger is location_type and headcount only, so any rooftop is treated as indoor. That is correct for a typical multi-storey roof and over-inclusive for a terrace under 20 feet. Narrowing it is a TRIGGER change and probably an intake-registry change, which is a product decision and not a note edit, so it is recorded in the note and in verification.qualification and deliberately NOT made here. No trigger, no intake field and no scenario output moves: the full suite is 808 tests before and after these three text edits. snapshot_date stays 2026-07-26: this artifact is published on the same day v2.7 was. The primary sources behind the unit correction were re-fetched on 2026-07-26, and that is recorded per rule in verification.evidence rather than here; last_verified_date remains null throughout. CARRIED FORWARD FROM nyc.v2.7. PUBLICATION ONLY: that bump MOVES NO EVALUATED OUTPUT and no expected output. It adds one config key and changes no rule, threshold, trigger, deadline or verification status. CONFIG: config.alert_offsets publishes the deadline_reminder offsets F-203 states as config rather than code (specs/F-203-deadline-alerts.md Outputs: latest_apply_date minus 7 days and minus 1 day). The values were already decided in F-203's own table, so this is publication rather than a product decision; what this file settles is the shape. It is keyed by alerts.alert_type and each type holds an object, so a later reminder kind and a later scheduling mechanism are both data additions to this file rather than changes to its schema. That is scoped to config on purpose: migration 001 constrains alerts.alert_type, so a new kind needs a forward migration too, and the note says so rather than promising data-only extensibility the persistence contract does not give. The offsets are PopEngine policy and the note says so in the same terms slack_warning_days uses, because presenting an internal reminder cadence as an agency deadline is the overclaiming failure F-102's verdict labelling exists to prevent. No engine code reads this key; the engine reads config by explicit lookup (slack_warning_days, business_day_math) and ignores the rest, which is already true of assembly_thresholds, so publishing it cannot move a verdict. PUBLICATION DATE: snapshot_date is 2026-07-26, the day this artifact was published. Every bump from v2.2 to v2.6 carried 2026-07-25 with the note "no source was re-fetched", which was consistent only because those republications happened on the same day; v2.7 is the first on a later day, and that justification turns out to have been reading snapshot_date as a source-fetch date. It is not one. F-206 defines it as published-on and not all-facts-verified-on, and F-206 Acceptance Criterion 5 keeps the snapshot publication date and the per-line verification date distinct, so this repo dates three different things separately: source fetches in docs/VERIFICATION-SOURCES.md (Rounds 1-2, 2026-07-22), artifact publication here, and per-fact verification in each rule's last_verified_date, still null throughout. Leaving 2026-07-25 while the status said published 2026-07-26 made the artifact contradict itself, and because plans persist snapshot_date immutably and F-206 forbids backfilling one, every plan generated from v2.7 would have displayed a publication date this file denies. No source was re-fetched and nothing here claims one was: that claim lives in the evidence record and in last_verified_date, neither of which moves. DOB-TALL-STRUCTURE-001 already declared that key and its own note_text already said "Deduplicates with the area/duration-based DOB rules", but no other rule carried it, so the key paired with nothing and the two rules emitted two findings for one DOB temporary-structure permit. (1) SCOPING: a new collected boolean battery_present gates battery_system_kwh, which previously had no asked_when and is nullable, so it was in scope and unanswered for every event. alert_offsets.note: PopEngine reminder policy, NOT an agency deadline; UI and alert copy must never present an offset as one. Each entry under a type schedules one alert at the item's latest_apply_date minus that many calendar days, so deadline_reminder sends at minus 7 and minus 1 (F-203 Outputs, which states these are config rather than code). Order is not significant. Keyed by the alerts.alert_type it schedules, so a later reminder kind (F-203's header names F-305 and F-413 reusing this plumbing) needs no change to THIS file's schema, only a new key, and because each type carries its own object a kind that does not schedule on days-before adds its own field without disturbing these. That is a claim about config alone: migration 001 constrains alerts.alert_type to deadline_reminder, slack_warning and dependency_unlocked, so a new kind also needs an ordered forward migration before a row can be inserted. slack_warning and dependency_unlocked are absent because they need no offset: they fire at checklist creation and at apply_after_date respectively.

engine_conventions: Tri-state evaluation; material unknown propagates to CONDITIONAL, never silently false.

A rule's kind (permit, insurance, notification, registration, eligibility, prohibition, dependency, classification, advisory, note) describes what the rule is. A persisted finding's kind is usually the same, with one exception: a classification rule (SAPO-SCOPE-001) emits a note finding. Persisted finding kinds are therefore permit, insurance, notification, registration, eligibility, prohibition, dependency, advisory, note.

Findings carry a disposition (REQUIRED, MAY_BE_REQUIRED, PROHIBITED_OR_INELIGIBLE, ADVISORY, NO_NEW_REQUIREMENT_IDENTIFIED). A classification rule emits a note finding with the NO_NEW_REQUIREMENT_IDENTIFIED disposition, retaining its rule id for provenance. These rule-domain kind/disposition names are stored in the plan-item schema's lowercase form (note, no_new_requirement); see ARCHITECTURE.

Top-level verdict stays four-state (FEASIBLE / FEASIBLE-AT-RISK / CONDITIONAL / INFEASIBLE) computed from per-finding deadline statuses (ON_TRACK / DEADLINE_APPROACHING / PUBLISHED_DEADLINE_MISSED / NOT_CALCULABLE / NOT_APPLICABLE). INFEASIBLE copy reads 'published deadline missed as scoped' — a missed filing window, not a claim of legal impossibility.
RESEARCH_REQUIRED deadlines are listed, rendered 'confirm with agency', excluded from verdict arithmetic.
OFFICIAL_CONFLICT rules render both readings and their sources; they never resolve silently.

A near-empty plan has no REQUIRED or PROHIBITED_OR_INELIGIBLE finding and renders 'No definite city event requirement identified from your answers.' plus its advisories and named confirmations. Deadline calculability does not change a finding's disposition.

deadline.qualification: Ten BUSINESS days, not calendar days, resolved against two independent primary sources: TPPN #07/96 'at least ten (10) business days in advance of the planned event', and AC Table 28-112.8 'at least ten work days prior to the event'. Inclusive on both, and DOB's current filing page adds 'The filing date of the online request counts as one of the days'. The superseded calendar-day reading came from DOB Code Notes (12.2016) 'must be submitted earlier than 10 days before the event' — that document says '10 days' and never 'calendar', disclaims itself as 'only a summary and overview ... not intended to substitute for the full text and meaning of any law, rule or regulation', names TPPN #07/96 as the governing notice, and describes the pre-DOB-NOW borough-office filing process, so it was the weakest of the three sources. Unit and boundary move together and both move the deadline EARLIER: taken alone the inclusive boundary would push this window one day LATER than the calendar-day value already known wrong, so publishing it without the unit would have made the rule less correct rather than more. The ten days are the FEE trigger; a separate three-business-day floor, anchored to the EVENT and not to the ten-day deadline, governs whether the filing is processed at all. That floor is published in display as TEXT rather than computed, following PARKS-EVENT-001's single-string precedent, because no deadline type in this schema expresses a business-day floor and adding one is a schema change that needs its own approved spec. Dating this window needs the holiday list config.business_day_math pins, which is deliberately unpublished (SPEC-CONFLICT #130; the decision and its evidence are recorded in apps/api/src/calendar.ts), so in the running product this deadline renders not_calculable with a null latest_apply_date and 'confirm with agency'. The fixture suite supplies an empty holiday list and therefore does compute a date; the two disagree by design and a green suite is not evidence this rule dates correctly in production. Min fee $250, +$100/day late.

notes: THE FDNY $415 IS THE VENUE'S PERMIT, NOT THIS EVENT'S COST, and earlier versions of this rule published it beside the TPA as though an organizer pays it. $415 is real and correctly cited — 2022 Fire Code Appendix A, FC A03.1(4), 'Assembly occupancies (places of assembly) ... Occupancy 75 to 149 $415.00' — but FC 105.6 attaches it to the permit 'to establish and operate a place of assembly', whose term 'shall be for a period not to exceed 1 year'. That is the party who operates the space, not the party who books it for one night. Note on periodicity, stated because it is easy to overstate: A03.1's preamble says 'All such fees are per year, except when based on frequency of inspection or hourly rate, as indicated', and item (4)'s own sub-label is 'Fire safety inspection/permit (frequency of inspection as required by code or rule)', which falls inside that exception — so A03.1 alone does not establish that $415 is annual, even though FC 105.6 caps the permit term at a year. NOT ESTABLISHED: which line FDNY bills for a one-off TPA event. The Fire Code's temporary-event line is a different item, A03.1(68) 'Street fairs and other public gatherings or gathering places', at $210 per hour for site-plan review and $210 per hour for fire safety inspection, and DOB's own page links the terminology ('also referred to in the Fire Code as a public gathering'). Nothing in Appendix A, Fire Code Chapter 1, or FDNY's Public Assembly Permit page (which says only 'Fee varies based on the number of occupants') says which applies. Confirm with FDNY rather than reading either amount as this event's cost. Citations are to the 2022 Fire Code: Local Law 47 of 2022 took effect 2022-04-15 and FDNY states the 2014 edition is no longer in effect, where these rows were item (3).

THE $250 IS DOB'S PUBLISHED FIGURE AND THE STATUTE LABELS IT DIFFERENTLY. DOB's current TPA page publishes 'The fee for a TPA is $250' with '$100 per day' extra inside 10 business days, and that is what this rule's fee displays. In Table 28-112.8 the row literally named 'Temporary place of assembly certificate of operation' is $130, while $250 AND the $100-per-day late fee AND the 'at least ten work days prior to the event' comment all sit together on the adjacent row named 'Temporary use letter for place of assembly'. NOT ESTABLISHED: which row DOB NOW bills for a TPA filing, or whether one filing draws both. Both are primary nyc.gov sources using different labels, no 1 RCNY rule reconciling them was located, and AC 28-112.1 leaves room for one ('shall not be valid until the fees prescribed herein or in rules have been paid'). DOB's operational figure is published as the fee an applicant pays and is kept for that reason; the discrepancy is recorded rather than resolved. The same row-label caveat applies to this rule's second source for the ten-day unit: the 'ten work days' comment is in Table 28-112.8, on the 'Temporary use letter' row, and DOB's public TPA page attributes all three facts — $250, $100/day, ten business days — to the TPA itself.

Thresholds: 75+ indoors OR ON ROOF TERRACES, the rooftop arm applying only to open spaces 20 FEET OR MORE above or below grade plane; 200+ outdoors. The 20-foot qualifier is load-bearing and DOB's webpage bullet drops it. BC 303.7 is the authority: 'A Certificate of Operation shall be required, as per Section 28-117.1, for the following assembly occupancies: 1. Indoor assembly occupancies used or intended for use by 75 persons or more, including open spaces at 20 feet (6096 mm) or more above or below grade plane, such as roofs or roof terraces. 2. Outdoor assembly occupancies used and intended for use by 200 persons or more.' So a roof or terrace UNDER 20 feet above grade plane is not swept onto the 75-person indoor side by 303.7(1); 303.7(2)'s 200-person outdoor threshold governs it instead, and a 90-person event on such a terrace would not trip this rule. This reaches the TEMPORARY instrument through code text rather than through a webpage: AC 28-111.6 states the TPA trigger in terms of 'the temporary use of space as a place of assembly', the Building Code Chapter 2 definition of PLACE OF ASSEMBLY resolves that term 'when such use requires a place of assembly Certificate of Operation pursuant to Section 303.7', and 303.7's test classifies the SPACE and draws no permanent/temporary distinction. The Fire Code follows the same definition ('as regulated by the Building Code'), so FDNY does not diverge. CONSEQUENCE THIS RULE DOES NOT ACT ON: height above grade plane is a real input to the trigger and this ruleset neither collects it nor branches on it, so the trigger treats a rooftop as indoor unconditionally. Narrowing it is a trigger and intake-registry change, not a note edit, and it is not made here.

An existing place-of-assembly approval does not by itself settle this. AC 28-117.1.3 (Local Law 2/2013): 'No change shall be made to a place of assembly that is inconsistent with the most recently issued place of assembly certificate of operation ... unless an amendment to such certificate is filed with and approved or accepted by the department', and it names any amendment to the plan for seating and other moveable furnishings as a change requiring one. Confirm with DOB whether this event's layout, occupant load and use fall within the venue's certificate.

Whether an existing approval removes the temporary filing itself is not published either way, and DOB 'approves TPA applications case by case', so this rule states the requirement without asserting an exemption.

Fire Code citations are to the 2022 edition (Local Law 47 of 2022, effective 2022-04-15); the 2014 appendix is superseded and numbered these rows differently.

verification.qualification: TWO EARLIER QUALIFICATIONS ARE NOW RESOLVED AND ARE NOT RESTATED HERE. The lead-time wording variance is closed: the unit is business days (TPPN #07/96; the Table 28-112.8 comment) and the bound is inclusive. And the roof-terrace clause IS established to reach the temporary instrument, through code text rather than through DOB's webpage bridge sentence — AC 28-111.6 states the TPA trigger as 'the temporary use of space as a place of assembly', the Building Code Ch. 2 definition resolves that term via 'Section 303.7', and 303.7 classifies the space without any permanent/temporary distinction. What remains UNESTABLISHED is the following, all of it silence in the sources rather than conflict between them, except where marked. (1) Whether a temporary filing is required at all at a venue that already holds a place-of-assembly certificate of operation is NOT PUBLISHED in either direction; the notes assert no exemption for that reason. (2) Which FDNY fee line applies to a one-off TPA event — the annual-permit line A03.1(4) or the public-gathering line A03.1(68) at $210/hr. Appendix A, Fire Code Ch. 1 and FDNY's own permit page do not say, so this rule publishes no FDNY amount as the event's cost. (3) Which Table 28-112.8 row DOB NOW bills for a TPA filing. THIS ONE IS A CONFLICT BETWEEN SOURCES, not silence: the row named 'Temporary place of assembly certificate of operation' is $130, while DOB's public TPA page publishes $250, which the statute attaches to the adjacent 'Temporary use letter for place of assembly' row. DOB's operational figure is the one published here. (4) The 20-foot-above-grade-plane qualifier in BC 303.7(1) means this rule's rooftop threshold is CONDITIONAL on a fact the intake does not collect; the trigger therefore treats any rooftop as indoor, which is correct for a typical multi-storey roof and over-inclusive for a terrace under 20 feet. Narrowing it is a trigger and intake-registry change and is deliberately not made here.
